title: Exact Worst-Case Rank Randomization Tests under Outcome Attrition
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the delivered package subfield with paper_score_ceiling 6.8 below the 7.4 field floor and salvageable=false; FPT/W[1], generated-support complexity, and applied informativeness remain unresolved, with local redundant-assumption and positioning findings unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The computational frontier is limited to XP versus variable-k NP-completeness for explicitly listed rationally weighted supports; FPT versus W[1]-hardness and uniform balance-generated supports remain open.

The projected paper score is constrained by this narrow computational scope and by the absence of power, informativeness, or applied evidence showing when the worst-case envelope is useful rather than vacuous.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the equality-inclusive weak-order maximum, unconditional validity, fixed-k and one-missing algorithms, effect inversion, an explicit-support CLIQUE reduction, and a succinct-CRE coefficient evaluator; two statement repairs were independently adjudicated and merged. D0.5 nevertheless capped the package at subfield (6.8) because it does not resolve FPT versus W[1]-hardness or complexity for uniform/generated supports and lacks power or applied-informativeness evidence. No counterexample was found, but the math and positioning panels still requested one redundant-assumption cleanup and targeted literature positioning, so the banked note is a research artifact rather than a formally verified result.
tldr: Attrition makes both a rank statistic and its randomization reference tail depend on missing sharp-null outcomes. For an explicitly listed rationally weighted fixed-count design, the exact worst-case Wilcoxon-midrank p-value is the maximum over a finite complex of complete weak orders, including equality faces. The envelope is finite-sample valid under arbitrary fixed treatment-indexed observation, computable in \(O((2n+1)^k n|\Omega|\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) time with a linear one-missing sweep, invertible over additive effects by a finite breakpoint scan, and NP-complete to maximize when \(k\) varies. For a succinct completely randomized design, the same ordinary-midrank maximum is computable in \(\left[\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\{2(g+j)+1\}\right]\operatorname{poly}(n,\ell_{\mathrm{CRE}})\) bit operations without listing \(\binom{n}{m}\) assignments, and is therefore polynomial for every fixed \(k\). A saved constrained cluster-randomization support is a concrete conditional-design consumer, provided the endpoint is prespecified and the support is not altered after attrition.
gap: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain a tractable extreme-completion formula under exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention, while general Fisher theory assumes that the statistic is evaluable. Neither line characterizes the completion optimizer for an arbitrary explicitly weighted support with ordinary midranks and active equality faces.
fill: The project proves the chamber representation and validity, identifies the fixed-\(k\) and variable-\(k\) computational boundary, performs exact additive-effect inversion, and gives a support-preserving constrained-cluster corollary.
